newsitem.title: USA: APS Holding drops after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: APS Holding drops after profit warning.

text.p: Shares of APS Holding Corp dropped almost 18 percent on Monday after the distributor of automotive replacement parts said it fiscal 1998 earnings will fall short of analysts' expectations.

APS said earlier that it is not seeing sustained improvement either in the operating performance of its Installers' Service Warehouse division or in the underlying business conditions of the automotive aftermarket.
APS posted a first quarter loss of $0.07 a share on net sales of $211.7 million, compared to a profit of $0.10 a share on net sales of $217.6 million a year ago.
Despite APS' earnings warning, analysts said they remain optimistic that the company will get back on track, perhaps within six months to about a year.
"This has not changed my opinion. They were a turnaround company last week. They still are a turnaround company," said Kenneth Salmon, an analyst with Cleary Gull Reiland & McDevitt.

Salmon said he expects the company will begin to show improvement in the second half of the year and could show positive year-over-year comparisons in the fourth fiscal quarter. He said he maintained an accumulate rating on the stock.
Earlier, APS also said it had obtained a waiver from its senior lenders on compliance with its consolidated leverage ratio requirement for the first quarter.
The waiver will be effective until July 15, APS said.

APS said it intends to propose to its senior lenders that the leverage ratio and certain other financial covenants in its credit agreement be amended, based on the company's first quarter results and the outlook for results for the remainder of its fiscal year 1998, which began January 26.
